newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Resources sees output up.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Resources sees output up.

text.p: Australian Resources Ltd said on Tuesday it mined more gold and copper in the quarter ended December 31 and was returning encouraging exploration results from its properties in Queensland and Western Australia.

"Gold production increased by 13 percent compared with the Sepember quarter, copper production was up by nine percent and the group's average cash operating cost per ounce of gold produced fell by 21 percent," Australian Resources chief executive Robert Ryan said in a statement.
The company said its share of production for the latest quarter totalled 55,029 ounces of gold and 5,920 tonnes of copper, mined at an average cash operating cost of A$265 per ounce.
This compares with 48,560 ounces of gold and 5,422 tonnes of copper at an average cash operating cost of $337 per ounce in the previous quarter, it said.

At the Selwyn mine in Queensland, exploration work yielded significant gold and copper results, including 14 metres at 5.95 grams a tonne of gold (from 2 metres) at the Blitzon prospect and 14 metres at 6.14 grams/t gold and 4.45 percent copper at
the Slate Ridge prospect, the compay said.
At Mount McClure in Western Australia, further encouraging results have been obtained at the Anxiety Bore propsect, with a best result of 12 metres at 31.96 gram/t of gold, it said.

Drilling results at the Gidgee mine, also in Western Australia, included 8 metres at 23.27 grams/t gold at the Butcherbird propsect and 1O metres at 14.42 grams/t of gold at the Emu Feather prospect, the company said.
